draft.shortGloss: to smell; to give off an odor
draft.emotion: attentive and curious, focusing on a scent or aroma
notes: Like English 'smell', used both transitively ('smell something') and intransitively ('smell good/bad'); alone without an adverb it often implies smelling bad.

senses.definition: To notice or perceive an odor with your nose.

examples.text: Μυρίζω τα φρέσκα λουλούδια στον κήπο.
examples.translation: I smell the fresh flowers in the garden.
examples.emotion: relaxed and appreciative of a pleasant natural scent

draftBefore.shortGloss: to smell; to give off an odor
draftBefore.emotion: attentive and curious, focusing on a scent or aroma
notes: In Greek, this verb is versatile: it can mean both the active act of smelling something (I smell the flower) and the passive state of giving off a scent (the food smells good).
It is often confused by learners with the noun 'μύτη' (nose); remember that 'μυρίζω' is the action performed by the nose.
